notes: From the homeowner's top-down plan + photo. House along the top; brick chimney projects into the middle bay; porch cover (26.5' x 10.5') over the chimney bay + right bay with its 6x6 cedar posts on the deck. Left end is OPEN (rail) — the 30' on the plan is the overall depth, not a wall. The wing's inner edge jogs: two 10'5" diagonals along the house side (a shallow angled bay) are framed here as a 2'-6" x 20' rectangular house bump on the wing's inner edge — diagonal cuts and the two angled rail/rim joints are not counted until it is measured. Plan says 8' high at the left, 6' at the right: frame set at 8', posts cut to grade. Widths set so they sum to the plan's 37' overall (10'6" wing + 10'6" chimney bay + 16' porch); the '9'' between the notch and the chimney could instead be its own bay, which would make the deck 46' wide — verify on site. PHOTOS (jobs/summit_point_photos): the existing deck is the 26.5' x 10.5' run along the big window wall plus the bay by the door — stained wood, black aluminum balusters, flat dark top rail, 6x6 posts; the wing exists too (photo 6: rail on its outer edge, brick house wall with the chimney on its inner edge) — the whole deck is demo'd. Existing translucent-panel cover on 6x6 posts stands on the deck by the door: take it down and reset it on the new frame (not priced — RFI). Existing boards run perpendicular to the house (diagonal in the wide section); the plan says both joists and boards run perpendicular, which cannot both be true — GSX frame kept (joists perpendicular, boards parallel); flipping to perpendicular boards is a rerun. PHOTOS 6-10: the existing top rail is a flat drink-rail cap (keep the drink rail). Photo 10: an existing straight stair, 4' wide, runs down along the house siding to a concrete pad — put on the right end (end:right) next to the house, one rail (house on the other side); confirm which end.
